Welcome to the Africa Digital Health Maturity Assessment Tool (ADHMAT). ADHMAT is Africa CDC's standardized instrument for assessing digital health at national level across the African Union Member States. This form brings together the structured maturity assessment and the Member State's own narrative, so that your country reports once, on one link.

Objective
To give Africa CDC and the Member State one consistent, evidence-based picture of national digital health: how mature the country's digital health systems are, and what progress, experience and context lie behind that picture, so that planning, investment and cross-country learning are better informed.

Specific objectives
1. Measure national digital health maturity against a common standard across five domains and digital payment systems.
2. Capture, in the Member State's own words, the progress, implementation experience, results, challenges and lessons behind the scores.
3. Establish a baseline that lets the country and Africa CDC track progress over time.
4. Identify strengths, gaps and national priorities, and where continental and partner support would add the most value.
5. Inform the State of Digital Health in Africa report and share lessons between Member States.

What happens with your answers. Your responses will be consolidated across Member States and will inform the State of Digital Health in Africa report. They help show where countries are strong, where support is needed and which lessons can be shared. This exercise supports learning and prioritisation and is not intended to rank Member States.

Africa CDC · Digital Health and Information System Division

One national assessment, four parts
1. Profile Information – the Regional Collaborating Centre and country, the assessment team, approval and data use. Only the essential fields are mandatory. At the end of this part you choose which module(s) you will complete in this session.
2. Quantitative Assessment – 373 Yes / No / N/A questions across five domains and a supplementary Digital Payment Systems section. Your domain results and overall result appear automatically at the end of the module.
3. Qualitative Insights – 14 narrative questions, all on one page, that explain the story behind your ADHMAT results. Each has a text box for a full written response.
4. Review and Submit – a final check that both modules are complete, then one submission.

Answering the questions
All questions are mandatory except the profile fields that are not essential. If a question does not apply to your country, or the information is not available, do not leave it blank: select N/A where offered and, in Qualitative Insights, write a short explanation of why it is not applicable or not available.

Working together on one link
Different colleagues can complete different modules: use Save & Return Later, keep the return code, and when you come back choose your module at the end of 1. Profile Information. Press Submit only once, after 4. Review and Submit shows both modules as Complete.

2. Quantitative Assessment · ADHMAT National Level (V2.5)
The Africa Digital Health Maturity Assessment Tool (ADHMAT) is Africa CDC's standardized instrument for assessing the maturity of a country's digital health systems across the 55 African Union Member States. This module covers the National level: 368 core questions in 5 domains plus a 5-question supplementary Digital Payment Systems section (373 questions in total). All questions are mandatory; answer N/A where a question does not apply at national level.

Scoring
Yes = 1  |  No = 0  |  N/A = Not Applicable at this level. Each question is answered at the relevant administrative level only. N/A answers are excluded from all score calculations - they do not count for or against the score.

Domain Coverage (National Level)
A. Digital Environment - 105 sub-questions
B. Architecture & Data - 140 sub-questions
C. Applications - 53 sub-questions
D. Analytics - 35 sub-questions
E. AI and Emerging Technology - 35 sub-questions
Digital Payment Systems (supplementary) - 5 sub-questions

Note on this layout: to reduce the number of sections, questions in this instrument are grouped by Domain first (A-E, then Digital Payment Systems), with each Domain shown as one section. Within a Domain's section, questions are grouped by the applicable cross-cutting sub-domain(s), shown via the green divider above each group - not every sub-domain applies to every domain.

How the Maturity Score Is Calculated
1. Each question is answered Yes, No, or N/A. N/A is excluded from scoring.
2. For each sub-domain within a domain (Leadership & Governance, Strategy & Investment, Legislation & Policy, Workforce, Standards & Interoperability, Infrastructure, Services & Applications), the tool counts how many questions were answered Yes.
3. % Yes = Yes count ÷ (Yes count + No count) × 100.
4. % Yes converts to a Maturity Level:
  L1 Nascent <40%  |  L2 Emerging 40–54%  |  L3 Established 55–69%  |  L4 Advanced 70–84%  |  L5 Optimized ≥85%
5. Each Domain's (A-E) score is the average % Yes across its applicable sub-domains.
6. The Overall score is the average of the 5 Domain scores. Digital Payment Systems is reported separately and is not part of the Overall score.
7. The five Domain results and the Overall result are calculated automatically and shown at the end of this module.

Section Header:
3. Qualitative Insights
About this module
Field Label:
3. Qualitative Insights

Purpose
This module collects qualitative evidence from AU Member States to complement the Africa Digital Health Maturity Assessment Tool (ADHMAT) and inform the State of Digital Health in Africa report. ADHMAT provides the structured assessment of national digital health maturity. This module therefore does not seek to reassess maturity or repeat information already captured through ADHMAT. Instead, it focuses on explaining recent progress, implementation experience, country context, results, challenges, lessons and future priorities.

Guidance for completion

  • Please provide one consolidated national response coordinated by the institution responsible for digital health.
  • Focus on developments during the reporting period specified by Africa CDC.
  • Where relevant, refer to findings from the latest ADHMAT assessment rather than repeating information already provided.
  • Prioritise concrete examples and implementation experience over general descriptions.
  • Where possible, provide supporting documents, data or links.
  • Clearly distinguish between measured results, observed experience and expert judgement.
  • If information is unavailable, please indicate this rather than estimating.
  • Do not provide personal, patient-level or otherwise sensitive health information.

All 14 questions are mandatory. Each has a text box for a full written response. If a question is not applicable to your country, or the information is not available, please write a short explanation of why rather than leaving it blank.

What were the three most significant digital health developments in your country during the reporting period?

For each, describe: what changed and why it was significant; what triggered or enabled the change; where and for whom it was implemented; any major implementation challenge and how it was addressed; any results or effects observed so far; and the main source of evidence.

Looking across your latest ADHMAT assessment, which two findings, strengths or gaps most require additional country context to understand?

For each, describe: the relevant ADHMAT finding or area; the factors that help explain the finding; whether these relate to policy, institutions, financing, workforce, infrastructure, implementation or another factor; any action taken since the assessment; and what the ADHMAT result alone may not fully capture.
